description.value: The study investigated associations between normal-range testosterone levels, emotion-recognition behavior, and amygdala and other brain activation during explicit facial-emotion recognition in healthy young males.

spans.text: Hence, we investigated whether normally distributed testosterone levels in healthy young males exert an influence on explicit emotion recognition and amygdala reactivity.

design.value: A cross-sectional correlational functional MRI study of 21 healthy right-handed males performing an explicit emotion-recognition task with facial expressions varying by emotion and poser gender.

spans.text: Twenty-one right-handed healthy males aged 21-33 years (mean age 25.1 years, S.D. = 3.5) were enrolled in the study.
We performed functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) using an explicit emotion recognition paradigm in healthy young males.

All subjects performed above average according to norms on several neuropsychological tasks taken from the computerized neuropsychological test battery (Gur et al., 1992) engaging nonverbal intelligence, cognitive flexibility, visual learning and memory.
